1. Incident Overview and Metadata
This blameless postmortem documents the SEV-1 production incident on August 14, 2026, affecting the Enterprise
Knowledge Assistant (EKA) API cluster. Grounded in Google SRE postmortem best practices, this review identifies root
causes, lessons learned, and preventive action items.
Attribute
Details
Incident Identifier
INC-84920 (SEV-1 Critical Availability Impairment)
Incident Title
Database Connection Pool Exhaustion on Knowledge Assistant API
Date & Duration
August 14, 2026 | 14:18 UTC – 15:00 UTC (42 minutes total duration)
Impact
98.4% of API queries failed with HTTP 500/504 errors; ~4,200 internal users affected; zero
data corruption.
Incident Commander
Alex Mercer (Staff SRE) | Comms Lead: Sarah Jenkins
2. Chronological Incident Timeline (August 14, 2026)
14:18 UTC: Scheduled Celery batch worker begins bulk ingestion of 15,000 engineering wiki documents.
14:22 UTC: Celery autoscaling launches 128 parallel worker containers. Workers connect directly to PostgreSQL,
bypassing the PgBouncer connection pooler due to a configuration drift in celery_settings.py .
14:25 UTC: PostgreSQL hits max_connections = 500 . All database connections saturate. API service requests
queue and fail.
14:27 UTC: Datadog synthetic probe triggers PagerDuty alert: "EKA Query API 5xx rate > 15%".
14:31 UTC: Incident Commander Alex Mercer declares SEV-1; war room assembled on Slack #incident-84920 .
14:36 UTC: Database DBA identifies 480 connections originating from Celery worker IP range.
14:41 UTC: IC issues mitigation command: kubectl scale deployment/celery-ingestion --replicas=0 .
14:46 UTC: Active connections plummet to 45. API p99 latency normalizes to 180ms. Health checks return green.
15:00 UTC: 15-minute monitoring soak window concludes with 0 errors. Incident declared resolved.
3. Root Cause Analysis (5 Whys)
Why did the API fail? PostgreSQL database rejected new connections, causing HTTP 500 errors.
Why did the database reject connections? The active connection limit (500) was fully saturated.
Why was the connection limit saturated? 128 Celery worker pods opened direct persistent database connections.
Why did Celery bypass the connection pooler? A recent PR updated the database host to the raw RDS endpoint
rather than the PgBouncer internal DNS.
Why did CI not catch this? Staging tests only execute against a single shared container without connection limits.
